assessment.summary: This laboratory study investigated the impact of the antibiotic oxytetracycline on the fecundity of Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes carrying kdr (L1014F) and ace-1 (G119S) resistance mutations. Using four laboratory strains (Kisumu, KisKdr, AcerKis, and AcerKdrKis), the researchers found that oxytetracycline significantly reduced fecundity in the KisKdr strain (homozygous for L1014F) compared to controls and susceptible Kisumu females. The study concludes that oxytetracycline induces a fitness cost specifically in mosquitoes carrying the L1014F mutation, which could have implications for vector control strategies.
exclusion_reasons: The study only uses laboratory strains (Kisumu, KisKdr, AcerKis, AcerKdrKis) and does not report genotype data for any African field populations.
